title: Utilities and environment for a glass studio: Charlottesville Gas service for furnaces, water and sewer connections, wastewater (slurry and grease) rules, stormwater, and state air-permit pointers
question: My glass studio needs a large natural gas supply for the furnace and glory hole, water for cold-working, and I will produce glass slurry and maybe cafe grease. How do I get City gas and water service, what are the fees and rules for what goes down the drain, and do I need an air permit?
office: City of Charlottesville Department of Utilities (Charlottesville Gas, water, wastewater, stormwater) and the Utility Billing Office; Public Works Engineering (erosion and sediment control, VESMP); Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (air permits, state)
summary: Charlottesville Gas is the City-owned natural gas utility; it serves most streets in the city. For a new or larger gas service, contact Utilities Outreach (434-970-3812, utilitiesoutreach@charlottesville.gov) to confirm availability and schedule a site visit, then file the electronic Gas Service Application and pay the connection fee by the emailed instructions. The published $340 connection fee (first 150 feet, with a furnace or water heater) is residential and rises to $1,950 on January 1, 2027; a commercial studio without a qualifying appliance gets a customized quote based on footage, excavation and pavement restoration, and commercial deposits are quoted by Utility Billing. Standard delivered pressure is 7 inches of water column; higher pressure (PSIG) for a furnace or glory hole is restricted to commercial and industrial customers and must be requested in writing with justification for the Gas Engineer's approval. The meter regulator vent needs 3 feet from openings and electrical equipment and 10 feet from fresh-air intakes. The City installs the line to the meter (about 4 weeks) and sets the meter; a licensed plumber or gas contractor pipes from the meter under a City gas permit, and the meter is unlocked the next business day after Building Inspections reports a passed final. Firm gas service is $10 a month plus $12.08 per 1,000 cubic feet for the first 3,000 cubic feet and falling tiers above, with a 'Summer Air Conditioning' rate and an interruptible rate for very large users. New water service costs a $30 service charge plus a meter set fee and a Water Facility Fee by meter size ($3,455 total for 5/8 inch, $8,275 for 1 inch, $25,465 for 2 inch) and a Sewer Facility Fee ($5,350 for 5/8 inch, $13,375 for 1 inch); sewer taps are requested through Utility Billing (434-970-3211) and a lateral replacement needs an NDS permit. The City publishes no industrial pretreatment or slurry-disposal page: glass grinding slurry should be settled and kept out of the sanitary and storm sewers, and a cafe follows the FOG program; ask Utilities before discharging anything but sanitary wastewater. Stormwater: an annual utility fee of $1.20 per 500 square feet of impervious area per month; land disturbance of 6,000 square feet or more needs an E&S plan ($200 application) and a VESMP permit, and over one acre a state Construction General Permit, with the state fees paid to the City. Air: DEQ's minor new source review rules exempt gaseous-fuel burning units under 50 million Btu per hour, but whether a glass melting furnace is exempt process equipment is a DEQ question; the City has no air program.

steps.step: Size the gas load and check that Charlottesville Gas can serve it
steps.who: Operator with the furnace builder or mechanical engineer; Utilities Outreach
steps.how: Add up the connected load (furnace, glory hole, garage or annealing kilns, any gas torches, water heater, cafe cooking) in Btu per hour, and decide whether the burners need more than the standard 7 inches of water column; most studio furnaces and glory holes are specified for elevated (PSIG) pressure. Email Utilities Outreach (utilitiesoutreach@charlottesville.gov) or call 434-970-3812 to check that gas is available at the address and to schedule a site visit; gas serves most streets in the city and limited parts of urban Albemarle. Higher delivered pressure is restricted to commercial and industrial applications and must be requested in writing with justification, for approval by the Gas Engineer or designee; limits include external fuel lines and the need for appliance regulators with an internal relief vented to the atmosphere. The City's installation requirements ask that the total gas connected load be reported to the Gas Unit. If City gas cannot serve the load, propane is a separate route: tanks and piping need the City gas permit and a Fire Marshal LP-gas permit (see glass_studio_fire_permits).

steps.step: Apply for the gas service line and meter and pay the connection fee
steps.who: Operator (or the property owner); Charlottesville Gas
steps.how: Submit the electronic Gas Service Application (the Survey123 form linked from the Gas Services page or www.charlottesville.gov/gas) for new service piping and a meter; a property that already has gas and only needs an account goes through Utility Billing instead. The City emails payment instructions; installation is not scheduled until the connection fee is paid. The published fee is residential: $340 for the first 150 feet with a furnace or water heater, rising to $1,950 on January 1, 2027 (an extra charge may apply for pavement restoration, and lines over 150 feet are quoted). A commercial studio without a qualifying appliance gets a customized quote based on footage, excavation type and pavement restoration. The service guide also lists a $30 meter connection fee, a $10 monthly charge and residential deposits ($250 heating, $75 non-heating); commercial deposits are quoted by Utility Billing and a commercial account cannot be put in a personal name. Deposits can be waived with a letter from another utility showing a good credit record. Rebates listed are for homes.
steps.fee: Residential: $340 (first 150 feet, qualifying appliance) until December 31, 2026, then $1,950; commercial or no qualifying appliance: customized quote; meter connection fee $30; monthly charge $10; commercial deposit by quote
steps.quote: Before installation can be scheduled and performed, the payment of a new gas service connection fee must be made.

steps.step: Prepare the meter location and let the City install the line and meter
steps.who: Charlottesville Gas (line to the meter, meter set); property owner (site conditions)
steps.how: In about 4 weeks the City installs the gas line from the street to the meter and calls VA811 itself; a gas technician sets the meter within about 10 days after that. Services are installed when the grade is within 6 inches of final between the main and the meter and the building exterior is finished around the meter location. Meter siting rules: the regulator vent at least 3 feet horizontally from equipment air intakes, operable windows and doors, and not under first-floor operable windows or doors; at least 10 feet from building fresh-air intakes (or the intake 3 feet below the vent); and 3 feet radial separation from electric meters, disconnects, outlets and rotating electrical equipment. Adjustments to the main or service after construction are at the owner's cost.
steps.deadline: About 4 weeks to the line, then about 10 days to the meter (service guide)
steps.quote: In about 4 weeks, we will install your gas line from the

steps.step: Have the house piping installed under a City gas permit and pass the two gas inspections
steps.who: Licensed gas or plumbing contractor; NDS Building Inspections; Charlottesville Gas
steps.how: Everything beyond the meter is the customer's: a licensed contractor pipes from the meter to the furnace, glory hole, kilns and torches under a Gas permit linked to the building permit (see glass_studio_building_mechanical). The Gas Services page describes a two-part inspection: an initial inspection of the installation with a pressure test of the piping, then a final inspection of the connections including the tie-in from the building piping to the meter; the permit holder schedules each (434-970-3182 or the portal) and reschedules a failed one. When the final passes, Building Inspections notifies Charlottesville Gas, and the meter is unlocked by the end of the next business day; meters cannot be unlocked before that notification.
steps.deadline: Meter unlocked by the end of the next business day after Charlottesville Gas receives the inspections office's notification
steps.fee: Gas permit: $75 minimum, then by project value (NDS Fee Schedule)
steps.quote: The initial inspection checks primary installation and performs pressure testing of the piping inside the home.

steps.step: Open the commercial gas account and understand the rate
steps.how: Use the online 'Application for Service: Business' on the Utility Billing forms page to open the account. Rates effective July 1, 2026 for a firm customer: $10.00 monthly charge; $12.0802 per 1,000 cubic feet for the first 3,000 cubic feet, $11.4332 for the next 3,000, $10.7862 for the next 144,000 and $10.1393 over 150,000 cubic feet, plus the purchased gas adjustment the rate report describes. A 'Summer Air Conditioning' rate ($9.4462 per 1,000 cubic feet, May through October) and an interruptible rate (annual minimum 1,200,000 cubic feet; $60 monthly, $8.7834 per 1,000 cubic feet for the first 600,000) exist; ask Utility Billing which schedule a furnace that runs continuously qualifies for. Gas transport rates apply only to very large volume customers.
steps.fee: Firm gas: $10.00 per month plus $12.0802 per 1,000 cubic feet (first 3,000 cubic feet) and lower tiers above; interruptible: $60.00 per month, annual minimum 1,200,000 cubic feet
steps.quote: First 3,000 cu. feet per 1,000 cu. feet

steps.step: Water and sewer: new or larger connections and their facility fees
steps.who: Operator or property owner; Utility Billing (434-970-3211); NDS Building Inspections (plumbing permit, lateral permit)
steps.how: An existing building with water service needs only the business account (deposit by quote). A new or upsized water service costs a $30 service charge plus a Water Meter Set Fee and a Water Facility Fee by meter size: 5/8 inch $325 plus $3,100 ($3,455 total); 1 inch $495 plus $7,750 ($8,275); 1.5 inch $565 plus $15,500 ($16,095); 2 inch $635 plus $24,800 ($25,465); larger sizes up to $249,145 for 6 inch and estimated above. A new sewer connection carries a Sewer Facility Fee by meter size: 5/8 inch $5,350; 1 inch $13,375; 1.5 inch $26,750; 2 inch $42,800. Apply for a sewer tap through Utility Billing; replacing a service lateral needs an NDS permit (434-970-3182). The Building Inspections department inspects water and sewer lines from the building to the utility tie-in or right-of-way, and the Utilities Standards and Design Manual (with Appendix F potable water and sanitary sewer specifications and Appendix D sewer details) governs the work. Monthly water and sewer service charges start at $12.50 each for a 5/8 inch meter, with volume rates per 1,000 cubic feet that differ by season.
steps.fee: New water service: $30 plus meter set fee plus Water Facility Fee ($3,455 total for 5/8 inch; $8,275 for 1 inch; $25,465 for 2 inch); Sewer Facility Fee $5,350 (5/8 inch), $13,375 (1 inch), $42,800 (2 inch); monthly service charge $12.50 water and $12.50 sewer for 5/8 inch
steps.quote: Call the Utility Billing for more information at 434-970-3211.

steps.step: Keep glass slurry, chemicals and grease out of the sewers
steps.who: Operator; Department of Utilities (wastewater); Rivanna Water and Sewer Authority (treatment)
steps.how: The City's collection system sends wastewater to the Rivanna Water and Sewer Authority's Moore's Creek plant. The City publishes no industrial pretreatment, sewer-use or slurry-disposal page, and City Code chapter 31 (Utilities) was not read. Plan on settling tanks or filtration for cold-working and grinding water so glass fines and polishing compounds (including any cerium oxide) are collected as solid waste rather than discharged, and ask Utilities in writing (434-970-3800, CVILLEUTILITIES@charlottesville.gov) whether any discharge beyond sanitary wastewater needs approval or a pretreatment agreement. Nothing but rain may go to storm drains: the City's MS4 program treats spills, process water and wash water as illicit discharges and asks that they be reported through its Pollution Prevention Report Form. A cafe follows the FOG program (scrape, cool and dispose of fats, oils and grease; the health department plan review asks for a grease trap where applicable).

steps.step: Stormwater utility fee, and erosion and stormwater permits if you disturb land
steps.who: Property owner; Public Works Engineering (E&S and VESMP); Utilities (stormwater fee)
steps.how: Every improved parcel pays the Stormwater Utility Fee twice a year on its impervious area: $1.20 per billing unit of 500 square feet per month (a 2,100 square foot example rounds up to 5 units and $72 a year); the owner can apply for a credit by maintaining a stormwater facility or for an adjustment if the billing is wrong. New paving or building that disturbs 6,000 square feet or more needs an Erosion and Sediment Control plan ($200 application fee; $150 amendment) and a Stormwater Management Plan (fees in the NDS and Public Works schedule) under City Code chapter 10; a Land Disturbance Permit and a VESMP permit are administered by Public Works Engineering and come after Final Site Plan approval. Disturbance of one acre or more needs the state Construction General Permit: the City has adopted the state fee schedule, and the CGP Registration Statement and fee are submitted to the City, payable to the City of Charlottesville.
steps.fee: Stormwater Utility Fee $1.20 per 500 square feet of impervious area per month, billed in June and December; E&S Plan application $200 (land disturbance of 6,000 square feet or more); E&S plan amendment $150; CGP fees per the state schedule, paid to the City
steps.quote: The City of Charlottesville adopted the state’s fee schedule. The fee form above is the same form on the DEQ website however it differs in that fees shall be made payable to the City of Charlottesville and submitted to the City for processing along with the CGP Registration Statement.

steps.step: Air permits: check the DEQ exemption for the furnace and keep the records
steps.who: Operator; Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (Blue Ridge Regional Office)
steps.how: Virginia's minor new source review rule exempts fuel burning equipment units (external combustion units) using gaseous fuel with a maximum heat input under 50,000,000 Btu per hour, and liquid or liquid-and-gaseous fuel under 10,000,000 Btu per hour, applied per unit per fuel type (in the aggregate in ozone nonattainment or maintenance areas). A studio furnace, glory hole and kilns are far below those inputs, but the rule lists exemptions by equipment type and process, and whether a glass melting furnace counts as 'fuel burning equipment' or as process equipment (the rule has separate rows for other processes) is DEQ's call; an owner claiming an exemption must keep records that show it. The DEQ air permit web pages refused automated reading, so ask DEQ's regional office directly, and confirm that exhaust from the furnace and any lead- or cadmium-bearing colors or batch materials raises no toxic-pollutant question. The City of Charlottesville has no local air permit program.
steps.quote: (4) Using gaseous fuel with a maximum heat input of less than 50,000,000 Btu per hour.

steps.step: Electric service, and who to call in an emergency
steps.who: Operator; Dominion Energy (electric); Charlottesville Gas dispatch
steps.how: Electricity in Charlottesville is from Dominion Energy, not the City; the Mandatory Inspections sheet says Dominion handles the service and inspections from the pole to the meter while the City inspects the rest. Report a gas smell or leak to Gas Dispatch at 434-970-3800 or 434-293-9164, 24 hours a day. Charlottesville Gas general operations (434-970-3800) handles installation schedules, relocating or removing a service and moving a meter.
steps.quote: Call Gas Dispatch at 434-970-3800 or 434-293-9164 to report a gas emergency 24/7.

caveats: The City's gas pages are written for homes. The $340/$1,950 connection fee is for residential services; commercial installations are quoted case by case. Whether a glass furnace is a 'qualifying appliance' and whether the 2027 increase changes commercial quotes is for Utilities Outreach to say.

No City page describes the higher-pressure (PSIG) service in detail: minimum load, metering, or cost. The rate pages list firm, interruptible, summer air conditioning and transport schedules; which applies to a studio furnace is not stated.

The City publishes no industrial pretreatment, sewer-use ordinance summary or slurry-disposal guidance. City Code chapter 31 (Utilities) and chapter 10 (Water Protection) were not read (Municode). The Rivanna Water and Sewer Authority's pretreatment rules were not researched.
Fees from the NDS and Public Works schedule (E&S plan $200, amendment $150, stormwater management plan fees) are read from a scanned PDF whose rows do not align cleanly.

DEQ's air permit pages (deq.virginia.gov) refuse automated readers (HTTP 403), so only the regulation text is cited. 9VAC5-80-1105 has many exemption rows beyond fuel burning equipment; it was not read in full, and the applicability of the minor NSR rule to a small glass furnace was not confirmed with DEQ.
Dominion Energy's commercial service process is outside the City and not researched.
The 2027 Utility Rate Report notes that gas is proposed to no longer offer $340 installations for qualifying appliances; the Gas Services page gives the January 1, 2027 date.
